newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bundestag begins four-day budget debate.
newsitem.headline: German Bundestag begins four-day budget debate.

text.p: The German Bundestag lower house of parliament began a four-day parliamentary debate on Tuesday on Finance Minister Theo Waigel's 1997 austerity budget, which will culminate in a final vote on Friday.

Irmgard Karwatzki, state secretary at the Finance Ministry standing in for Waigel -- absent due to illness -- told deputies that the "savings and consolidation budget" would meet entry criteria for European monetary union.

Karl Diller, finance spokesman for the opposition Social Democrats, hit out at Waigel for budget "trickery" in drafting the budget and warned that, like this year, holes would open up in financial projections and force up state borrowing.

The budget foresees federal spending of 440 billion marks, down 2.5 percent on 1996. Waigel has said that would enable Germany to achieve a combined budget deficit of 2.5 percent of gross domestic product, below the Maastricht treaty's three percent limit.
